front.title: An Architecture for Distributed Bandwidth Management Using TE Tunnels and Policies

abstract.t:
Traffic Engineering (TE) deployments steer traffic over provisioned TE constructs and associate bandwidth with them. Examples include point-to-point and point-to-multipoint (P2MP) Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic Engineering (RSVP-TE) tunnels, Segment Routing (SR) Policies, and Multipath TE (MPTE) constructs that are provisioned as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). As demand changes, operators automatically resize the bandwidth allocated to each construct based on measured traffic, a function commonly called auto- bandwidth, but no common description of this practice exists across TE technologies.
This document defines an architecture for distributed bandwidth management, in which the originator of each TE construct evaluates and adjusts its bandwidth without central coordination, and can offload computation and bandwidth estimation to an external entity. The architecture is independent of the forwarding plane and assumes a signaling plane, such as RSVP-TE, that provides per-link bandwidth accounting, admission control, and preemption. It covers traffic measurement, bandwidth estimation, adjustment, periodic and event- driven evaluation, and the management of a service carried by multiple concurrently usable tunnels (Container Tunnel management). Technology-specific signaling, data models, path computation, and estimation algorithms are outside its scope.
This document defines no new protocol extension or wire encoding.
